speaker: Doctor
text:
I see you have a history of easy bruising and persistent bleeding after your wisdom tooth extraction; have you experienced similar bleeding episodes during childhood or after minor injuries?

REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count with Platelet_Counter
REQUEST TEST: Prothrombin_Time and Partial_Thromboplastin_Time

Please let me know your answers and if you are willing to undergo these tests.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hematocrit: 35%, Leukocyte_Count: 8,500/mm3, Platelet_Count: 160,000/mm3; Prothrombin_Time: 15 sec, Partial_Thromboplastin_Time: 60 sec

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient was brought in by his mother for persistent bleeding following elective removal of wisdom teeth. The bleeding from the surrounding gums was minimally responsive to multiple gauze packs. The patient also has a history of easy bruising. Family history includes the patient's uncle who had similar issues with bleeding and a history of easy bruising and joint swelling.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Persistent bleeding from gums following tooth extraction. I also have History of easy bruising, Family history of similar bleeding problems and joint swelling. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Gastroenteritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is incorrect; gastroenteritis is an infection of the stomach and intestines and does not cause bleeding gums or easy bruising. Given your family history and joint swelling, we need to check your clotting factors. REQUEST TEST: Coagulation_Panel (PT, aPTT, INR) and REQUEST TEST: Factor_VIII_and_VII_assay. Can you confirm if those joint swellings were painful or associated with fever?

speaker: Doctor
text: The prolonged aPTT (60 seconds) suggests a problem with the intrinsic pathway, likely affecting hemophilia A or von Willebrand disease. Did you experience any bleeding into your joints or muscles spontaneously, and do you have any personal or family history of diagnosed hemophilia? REQUEST IMAGES: MRI of affected joints if available.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Previously healthy, takes no medications. Social history: The patient is a high school student with no history of smoking, alcohol, or drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hemophilia A. Based on the prolonged aPTT, family history, and joint bleeding symptoms, this is the most likely diagnosis; please confirm with the Factor VIII assay results.
